item.title: 'Hungry to win.' Simsbury football has been the turnaround story of 2026
item.description: Simsbury football coach Jim Caouette talks with Hunter Woolf during a 27-7 win over Newington at Holden Field in Simsbury on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) SIMSBURY - The leaves are off the trees beyond the north end zone of Holden Field, but the Simsbury Trojans who play there remain at peak. With a 27-7 win over Newington on Friday night, Simsbury football improved to 7-1. Which means the town that is home to the Pinchot Sycamore, the state's biggest tree, is home to the team enjoying the season's biggest turnaround in Connecticut high school football . Mark the rings on the trunk: Simsbury was 1-9 a year ago, 2-8 in 2024 and 1-9 in 2023. Heading into 2026, the team had its third head coach in as many years come through the door. He's proven to be a good one. Jim Caouette, the longtime defensive coordinator at Holy Cross-Waterbury and one-time head coach at Avon, a ball of energy and new schemes on both sides of the ball, harnessed a 19-strong group of seniors hungry to win as they once did before they got to high school. Another advantage: Simsbury moved down a rung on the Central Connecticut Conference ladder, from Tier 2 to Tier 3. There, the Trojans have not lost since dropping their season opener to Middletown, 40-35. They've won seven straight, the second-longest streak in program history, and stand No. 4 in the CIAC Class L playoff rankings. They are on course to match the 9-1 of 2019, the last time Simsbury football reached the postseason. It had been one long dry spell since, a meager 12 wins across five seasons. This fall, the Trojans pushed all that to the curb. "I think last year and years prior we've just been beating ourselves up on our own; it's been 'Simsbury versus Simsbury' is what the coaches say," remarked senior captain and lineman Brett Osborne. "So I think we've really learned how to take it in and move forward instead of taking steps backwards." The Trojans have two games remaining with E.O. Smith and Glastonbury. Their plus-6 shift in victories so far puts them ahead of several other teams of marked improvement this season. New London (3-7 to 8-0), Tolland (1-8 to 6-2) and Thames River (2-7 to 7-1) increased by five wins. Lewis Mills/Wolcott Tech (2-8 to 6-2), New Milford (1-9 to 5-3) and the SMSA Co-op (1-9 to 5-2) each improved by four wins thus far. Of note: New London and Thames River are also under new coaching regimes. Jack Cochran is back at New London after being out of the game for 13 years. Will Henton is in his first head coaching position with the Thames River co-op of Grasso and Norwich Tech. Caouette led Avon for three seasons, 2013 through 2015, and went 23-9. He is better known as the assistant coach who oversaw the Holy Cross defense for the next decade while his son Drew became the school's top all-time passer . item.title: Stephen Jones Admits Dallas Must Learn To Close Games Now
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys barely survived a close battle with the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, but the victory does not mean the job is done. Stephen Jones, the team’s co-owner, made it clear that the franchise still has a key lesson to learn after the 27-23 win. The game felt eerily similar to the loss against Arizona the week before, and the team needs to fix its habit of letting leads slip away. Jones did not mince words about the state of the squad. “I think it’s something that — it’s a learning experience. I still think we’ve got a long ways to go,” Jones said. The team has to learn how to win and how to close out games, which remains a major problem for this group. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer agrees with this assessment and knows the team must do better things to succeed. Penalties Are Killing Dallas The most glaring issue on the field was a lack of discipline that nearly cost the Cowboys the game. Pro Football Network reported that Dallas’s 14 penalties totaling 153 yards erased over 100 yards of total offense. Former NFL star Chad Johnson was furious about the sloppy play and warned the team that they cannot have so many penalties if they want to win. Johnson compared the team’s behavior to the Oakland Raiders of the 80s and 90s. The worst moment came when inactive linebacker DeMarvion Overshown ran onto the field in street clothes to celebrate a big play. Referee Clay Martin called an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for the non-uniform player in blue sweats and a stocking cap. “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. We had a non-uniform player in blue sweats and a stocking cap come onto the field to celebrate. That’s a 15-yard penalty,” the official announced. After a mistake shifted Dallas from its own 33-yard line to the 18, Indianapolis tied the game following a three-and-out. Closing The Game Remains A Struggle Even with a strong offensive showing, the Cowboys could not put the game away when they had the chance. Quarterback Dak Prescott called the offensive penalties “purely unacceptable” after the game, highlighting the frustration within the locker room. The team has made good plays, but drives often end up the way no one wants them to end in terms of moving the ball and scoring. “In this particular case, last week was no different closing the game out. We’re just not getting that done right now,” Jones noted regarding the struggles to finish drives. The Cowboys now sit at a 4-5 record on the season and must clean up these mistakes quickly. With the playoff race still alive, the team trails the New York Giants by just 2.5 games for first place in the NFC East. Dallas faces a tough test next as they prepare to play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 4:25 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium.

item.title: Real Madrid midfielder set to undergo tests after suffering injury in national team camp
item.description: Real Madrid midfielder set to undergo tests after suffering injury in national team camp The international break has just begun but it appears that disaster has already struck as far as Real Madrid are concerned. One of their key players, Aurelien Tchouameni has suffered an injury while away with the France national team, reports L’Equipe . Tchouameni injured again Tchouameni missed the start of the 2026/27 season due to an injury he had sustained with France at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. While he returned to action in September, new France manager Zinedine Zidane opted not to call him up to the squad during the previous international break, giving him time to fully recover his fitness and rhythm. Injured again? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Since then, Tchouameni has done exactly that, once again establishing himself as an important player for Los Blancos , and earning a recall to the French national team for their upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Italy and Turkiye. However, as per the report, Tchouameni was forced to stop training during today’s session after suffering a groin injury. Having been unable to complete the session, the 26-year-old midfielder will now undergo tests to determine the nature and severity of the injury. Once that is done, it will be decided whether Tchouameni will travel to Italy with the rest of the France squad return to the club. Concern for Real Madrid As already mentioned, Tchouameni has once again become an integral part of the Real Madrid setup under Jose Mourinho. A key cog in Mourinho’s system. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The French midfielder is key to providing the defensive solidity on the field operating alongside someone like Bernardo Silva in the double pivot. Since returning from injury, he has made ten appearances for Real Madrid in all competitions, starting eight of those, indicating the faith that Mourinho has in him. As such, if Tchouameni is injured with the France national team camp, it will come as a big blow for Los Blancos heading into an important stretch of the season. For now, those at Valdebebas will be eagerly awaiting results of the French international’s medical examinations and hoping that the groin issue he is dealing with does not turn out to be something serious.

item.description: For the Wolverines, there were plenty of takeaways from their first loss of the season. If they want to beat the top teams in the country, they can’t shoot 25% from 3-point range. They can’t commit 27 fouls and give the opponent 36 free-throw attempts. They can’t have starting guard Trey McKenney go scoreless for an entire half. And they can’t have the entire bench combine for just eight points on 2-for-12 shooting like it did in the 85-77 setback against UConn in Boston. “I don't think we have somebody we think can come in and just — like Trey came off the bench last year, he was a scorer. L.J. Cason came off the bench last year. We knew we were going to get points from those guys,” Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. said. “I think this year it’s still kind of a wait and see because we don't have a bunch of guys who've done it so far.” One of the many things that made last season’s national title team so great was its reliable depth. Michigan had multiple reserves who could score in double figures on any given night. Whenever the Wolverines went to their bench, there wasn’t much drop-off and the second unit often helped create separation on the scoreboard. item.title: Gautam Gambhir's infamous Oval row resurfaces as groundsman Lee Fortis leaves Surrey due to disciplinary proceedings
item.description: Gautam Gambhir's infamous Oval row resurfaces as groundsman Lee Fortis leaves Surrey due to disciplinary proceedings originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Lee Fortis has left Surrey after disciplinary proceedings into his conduct. He was placed on indefinite leave in July following a row with an ECB employee. Fortis clashed with Gautam Gambhir at the Oval during the 2025 England vs India Test series. The two had a confrontation during practice when Gambhir suggested Fortis was "just a groundsman". Why did Lee Fortis leave Surrey as the Kia Oval's groundsman? The man at the centre of one of the more viral confrontations of India's 2025 tour of England has lost his job. Lee Fortis, head groundsman at the Oval since 2012, has left Surrey following disciplinary proceedings into his conduct. Telegraph Sport reported on Tuesday that Fortis was placed on indefinite leave in late July after a row with an England and Wales Cricket Board employee, the day before MI London played London Spirit in the Hundred at the Oval. He then had what the paper described as a robust conversation with Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy, the former South Africa fast bowler, and did not return to work for the rest of the summer. His departure was confirmed through his LinkedIn page, which now states he left in October and is open to work. Exclusive: Lee Fortis departs following row with ECB employee in July and was known within the game for a robust communication style @willis_macp has story 👇 https://t.co/aB9O8BZSnm https://t.co/3cSoIWucaZ — Telegraph Cricket (@TeleCricket) November 10, 2026 A Surrey spokesman told the Telegraph that Fortis had left the club and that they wished him well. The Cricket Regulator was reported to have opened a case into the matter but declined to comment, and the findings of the disciplinary proceedings have not been made public. The July incident was not isolated, with Fortis having built a reputation for a direct manner toward both his own staff and visitors to the ground. MORE: 'They don't have to see my face': Usman Khawaja reveals why he waited until Australia retirement to expose Sandpapergate What happened between Gautam Gambhir and Lee Fortis at the Oval? For an Indian audience, Fortis is known for one exchange. During India's 2025 tour, he and Gautam Gambhir clashed over access to the Oval square, and the confrontation was filmed and shared worldwide within hours. Gambhir's response became the line that followed Fortis around. "You're just a groundsman, nothing beyond that," the India head coach told him, in a dressing-down that drew criticism in England and considerable support in India. India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak backed his colleague afterward, describing Fortis as arrogant. The episode fed into a wider narrative about Gambhir's combative touring style, and it is why his name has resurfaced alongside news of a groundsman's exit from a county club.

item.title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. Their 118.1 defensive rating ranks 26th, and they’re shooting only 32.5% from three as a team. I mean, we spent all of last season watching this team lose 56 games, and now we’re basically back to the same conversation. They’ve changed coaches, brought in young players, and tried different lineups, but we’re still wondering when this franchise is going to compete again. And Joe Dumars has some pretty important decisions coming. There’s already been trade interest in Murphy and Herb Jones , Zion keeps appearing in trade discussions , and the Pelicans have a couple of young players who could be worth more than some established veterans. So here’s how I’d rank the Pelicans’ seven most valuable trade assets right now, based on their production, age, contracts, injury history, and what I think another team would actually pay for them. item.description: With Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk turning 35 just ahead of the start of the 2026-27 season and now into the final year of his contract, questions about what the future might hold for the Premier League legend have of late begun to push their way into the conversation. For Van Dijk, though, the focus remains on the present. Or at least that’s what he’s telling anyone who asks, with the Dutch international—who pulled out of his country’s latest round of friendlies and will miss national team duty for the first time since 2020—being pressed on the issue this week. “I feel good, but it’s not about me at the moment,” he said when asked if he sees himself continuing at the highest levels, and at Liverpool in particular, beyond the current campaign. “Let’s see, but I’m not in any panic. I want to keep playing and to continue what I’m doing. “So let’s see what the season brings, but I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, then that’s the case. If not, then I will have to go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress about it or anything.” While Liverpool look to have gotten back on track under new manager Andoni Iraola, they probably aren’t quite at the stage yet where they could be counted as title contenders—and if that’s going to take another year, we’ll be hoping Van Dijk is around to take part in another title race. And in the meantime, too, even if the Reds are currently nine points back of Arsenal, there are other prizes they will expect to seriously push for this season—from the League Cup and FA Cup to the Champions League—and Van Dijk remains key to any success they do have.

Over the course of six months, five candidates rose to the top in the Reds' Sal Stewart, Mets' Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, Cardinals' JJ Wetherholt and Rockies' TJ Rumfield. In the end, it was Stewart who was named the NL Rookie of the Year honor as the Baseball Writers Association of American announced the award on Monday night. Stewart took home the honor on the strength of his 32 home runs and 112 RBI, which led all NL rookies, along with 87 runs, a .787 OPS, 25 doubles and 15 stolen bases. Stewart earned 20 of the 30 possible first-place votes. The Mets' Benge ended up as the runner-up with seven first-place votes, three second-place votes and 12 third-place designations. One of those votes for Benge to receive the top honor was mine. When the BBWAA assigned its award designations to the writers in early August, the Rookie of the Year race appeared to be a two-horse race between Stewart and Wetherholt. But over the the final two months of the season, Benge's kick provided further intrigue. That's why the season is an endurance race. And by the completion of the 2026 season, I believe Benge had done enough in all facets of the game to warrant the top slot in the Rookie of the Year vote. Stewart's explosive bat made him a top contender. The Reds first baseman had the second-most RBI and eighth-most home runs in the National League while he slashed .263/.330/.457. But defensively, he posted a -2 outs above average and a negative first-base receiving score. Wetherholt, who finished third in the voting, proved he had one of the best gloves in all of baseball, boasting a +25 outs above average that trailed only Cubs MVP frontrunner Pete Crow-Armstrong for the best mark in baseball. While batting atop the Cardinals' lineup, the second baseman led all rookies with 89 runs, while adding 17 home runs, 51 RBI and 14 stolen bases but posting an unassuming .242/.339/.365 slash line in 139 games. Benge provided the best of both worlds in terms of offense and defense despite a slow start through the opening two months, which hurt his case in the early going. Benge opened with a .189 batting average and .525 OPS through the month of April. He slashed .299/.363/.457 over the final five months. item.title: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler out for Season
item.description: The Miami Dolphins will be without one of their defensive leaders for the remainder of the 2026 season. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Dolphins defensive tackle and team captain Zach Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps during Sunday’s loss to the Detroit Lions and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Despite the injury, Sieler remained in the game and played 49 snaps on defense and special teams. He is expected to make a full recovery in five to six months. Sieler, 31, has been a fixture on Miami’s defensive line since being claimed off waivers from the Baltimore Ravens in 2019. He recorded consecutive 10-sack seasons in 2023 and 2024 and signed a three-year contract extension with the Dolphins in 2025. Sieler recorded two sacks this season, both of which came against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With Sieler sidelined, Miami is expected to lean more heavily on its younger defensive tackles, including former first-round pick Kenneth Grant, fourth-round selection Jordan Phillips, and seventh-round pick Zeek Biggers, all of whom have been part of the defensive line rotation this season. The news also effectively ends any speculation about a potential trade involving Sieler ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. Prior to the injury, he was among the veteran players who could have drawn interest from contending teams.

item.title: Ford brings music, motorsports, Mustangs to Daytona for Veterans Day
item.description: Daytona Beach , Florida ― Veterans Day is getting a Ford V-8 soundtrack.The inaugural Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic roars onto the high banks of Daytona International Speedway Wednesday night, Nov. 11, with big names from the racing and music worlds. Sponsored by Ford in collaboration with NASCAR, Blue Star Families, IMSA and HSR, the USA Network-televised event will feature a dozen of Ford’s top racing drivers going head-to-head in Mustang Dark Horse R Challenger race cars representing six military services. Each Mustang bears a livery inspired by an iconic military vehicle, from the F-22 stealth fighter to the Abrams tank to a Navy destroyer. If the V-8 soundtrack isn’t enough, the Zac Brown Band will bring its country tunes to the Daytona stage along with Russell Dickerson, Jo Dee Messina, Brittney Spencer and Warren Zeiders. “From building submarine chasers for the Navy in World War I, to our role as the ‘Arsenal of Democracy’ during World War II — when tanks, jeeps and B-24 Liberator bombers rolled off our assembly lines — to modern initiatives supporting veteran hiring and military families, this commitment is woven into the very fabric of who we are,” said Ford in a press release. “This Veterans Day, Ford is strengthening that commitment, honoring those who keep our country safe and the families that serve beside them.” The Classic will benefit six nonprofits: Blue Star Families, Camp Southern Ground, DAV (Disabled American Veterans), Team Rubicon, Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS) and The Travis Manion Foundation. The first-of-its-kind motorsports-palooza at Daytona unites racing, music, charity and service in honor of the nation’s military community. But like an Army-Navy game, competition is at its heart — pitting Ford’s finest drivers representing each military service. The driver teams: U.S. Army: NASCAR Cup Series’ driver Brad Keselowski and sports car expert Joey Hand. The car’s livery is inspired by the Abrams tank. Hand’s father is a 20-year National Reserve veteran; Sargeant’s grandfather served 30 years in the Navy; and Muniz’s (a former child actor) father is a Navy and Air Force veteran.
